study type: Longitudinal cohort with animal and in vitro assays
exposure: colonization of short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) producers
outcome: oxygen consumption rate of host cells
cohort: The study analyzed 346 fecal samples from children aged 6-36 months (112 non-AD, 110 mild AD, and 124 moderate to severe AD) from the Longitudinal Cohort for Childhood Origin of Asthma and Allergic Disease birth cohort.
finding: Disordered gut microbiome development and colonization of SCFA producers in children with atopic dermatitis led to abnormal SCFA production, increased IgE levels, and a butyrate deficiency that negatively impacts host cell oxygen consumption.
